A sweet frequency zone is a range you repeatedly find comforting. The spectrum shows which frequencies a sound contains. Your listening ratings help explore which ranges feel good to you, in a particular mood and setting.

UNDERSTAND THE ZONES

The pitch range and the beat are separate.

A sound-frequency zone groups nearby audible pitches. A binaural beat difference is the spacing between the tones sent to each ear. For example, 168.5 and 171.5 Hz sit around 170 Hz, with a 3 Hz difference. That does not mean the recording contains an audible 3 Hz tone.

These clusters come from the 30-second excerpt of your first reference. They describe what is present in a sound you selected; they do not tell us which part caused comfort or establish a preferred range. The handpan and bowls contain changing notes and broader textures.

Explore your own zones: compare nearby settings at a similar low volume, keep the sound type and beat difference consistent, and save how each felt. Look for repeated comfort in the same context, including neutral and uncomfortable sessions. The frequency-zone map below groups those observations without filling untested ranges.

Current player: 100–600 Hz base tone and 0–12 Hz difference in 1 Hz steps. It cannot reproduce the lower 82 Hz pair or its 0.5 Hz spacing. The map uses 50 Hz columns for readability; those boundaries are display choices, not discovered comfort thresholds. This prototype does not measure brain activity or establish migraine benefit.

These are acoustic carrier differences, not measurements of a person’s brain rhythms. We have no EEG or controlled pain-response data for these recordings. The handpan and bowl recordings are not assigned a beat by subtracting unrelated peaks.

PROVENANCE & METHODS

Keep the measurement in context.

These are three 30-second excerpts: the first recording at 32:48–33:18, and the handpan and singing bowls at 01:00–01:30. They cannot represent every passage in the full recordings.

The audio was decoded as stereo at 44.1 kHz. Frequency spectra use Hann-window averaging; the close-ups use the complete excerpt. The spectrogram trades some frequency precision for time detail.

No brain-response measurements were collected. The research does not establish a universal frequency that maximizes comfort or treats migraine.
